executive_assessment.text: Municipal examples distinguish socioeconomic vulnerability from modeled flood exposure; informal riverbank communities face additional housing and coping constraints.
Social protection cannot yet fully scale for climate shocks. Local plans and ALBAdapt monitoring/early-warning ambitions add institutional detail but do not prove delivered risk reduction.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-10 reports: The CCDR's socioeconomic-vulnerability list includes Dropull, Këlcyrë, Përmet, Kolonjë, Fushë Arrës and Mallakastër among the highest-ranked municipalities.
Source dated 2024-10 reports: The CCDR's ranked high-flood-exposure list names Fier, Lushnje, Shkodër, Roskovec, Divjakë, Rrogozhinë and Vau i Dejës.
Source dated 2024-10 reports: Flooding has worsened exposure for disadvantaged informal communities along riverbeds in Tirana, Durrës, Vlora, Shkodër and Lezha.
Source dated 2025-10 reports: NAP profiles flag hotter, drier summers in Durrës; erosion, landslides and shortages in Elbasan; floods across Fier; and flood/intense-rain risk in Kukës.
Source dated 2025-10 reports: Future urban risk is rated very high for Tirana, Durrës, Vlorë, Fier, Shkodër, Elbasan and the coastal belt across four subsectors.

Source dated 2025-10 reports: The NAP reports eight municipal plans developed with technical staff, data collection and capacity-building; each identified about 85 adaptation measures and 45 priorities on average.

Source dated not stated reports: ETMI reports Shkodër's local adaptation plan was delivered in 2025, with sector analyses, prioritized actions and a governance and monitoring framework supported by stakeholder engagement.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 11 of 12 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No pre-existing ALB country dossier was present under countries/ in this worktree; this is new-country Phase 2 extraction.
The National Security Strategy's climate-security passage is global risk framing, not an Albania-specific causal finding; no armed-conflict or climate-related violence link was established.

The English Ministry-hosted National Security Strategy file returned HTTP 502; the official Albanian PDF was opened and translated. The full Shkodër local adaptation plan was not linked, only its project summary.
No accessible source linked conflict or insecurity to weaker climate adaptation or disaster-service delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The global climate-security strategy passage is excluded from substantive Albania evidence. No complete Albania-specific climate–violence or reverse insecurity chain is supported.
Municipal vulnerability scores reflect population change and market access; flood rankings use a modeled event. Neither is a count of people already harmed.
